title: Session Pacemaker: Latency-aware KV Packer for Streaming Chat
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: We need a lightweight, deployment-safe batching heuristic ("Session Pacemaker") that packs streaming chat requests into micro-batches while respecting per-request latency budgets and KV-cache memory constraints. The goal is to reduce per-token cost and GPU tail utilization without increasing 95/99th latency beyond configured SLOs. This ticket designs the heuristic, implements it in the streaming batcher, and validates behavior in synthetic and shadow-prod workloads.

Background: Current continuous batchers optimize throughput by aggregating turns into large windows, but they can cause KV cache growth and GPU memory spikes for long contexts, and they sometimes hold low-latency interactive sessions until batch windows fill. We must balance three constraints: per-session latency budgets, KV cache memory footprint, and overall GPU utilization (to avoid OOMs and noisy neighbor effects).

Problem statement:
- Streaming chat workloads have a mixed distribution: many short interactive sessions with tight latency budgets and a tail of long-history sessions that cause large KV cache growth.
- Existing heuristics either favor throughput (leading to latency spikes on p95/p99) or favor strict latency (leading to poor GPU utilization).

Design goals:
1) Respect per-request latency SLOs (configurable by route): ensure median and p95 latency increases are minimal for interactive sessions.
2) Bound active KV cache allocation per-GPU by packing fragments (sessions) such that aggregate KV memory stays within safe headroom.
3) Opportunistically coalesce turns from sessions with compatible context shapes to improve kernel utilization.
4) Graceful fallback: when KV pressure is high, favor small-batch fast-paths and spill low-priority long-history sessions to secondary model variants.

Proposed heuristic (Session Pacemaker):
- Each incoming streaming request is tagged with (priority, latency_budget_ms, context_length_tokens_est).
- Maintain 3 concurrently open micro-queues per GPU slab: fast-path, balanced, long-context.
- Admission: place requests into fast-path if latency_budget <= 200ms and context_length_est <= 512; balanced for median requests; long-context otherwise.
- Packing policy per micro-queue (every 8ms cadence or on N requests):
  * Fast-path: form micro-batches of up to M_fast tokens or until a per-request deadline (min remaining latency budget across members) would be violated. Target: batch sizes 1-8 requests.
  * Balanced: allow larger aggregation up to M_balanced tokens, but enforce per-slab KV_memory_headroom threshold H (e.g., 70% of allocable KV region). If headroom < H, reduce target batch token cap by 50% and prioritize earliest-deadline-first.
  * Long-context: prefer single-request or 2-request batches; if several long-context requests share a common prefix hash (detected by prefix fingerprint), pack them to reuse KV segments.
- KV packing: when assembling a batch, compute combined KV token footprint; if combined footprint exceeds per-slab headroom, apply one or more of: (a) evict cold KV fragments based on LRU+session-score, (b) split the batch into smaller sub-batches, (c) reroute some requests to a spill pool (secondary model variant or CPU staging).
- Dynamic pacing: monitor observed p95 latency per-route and per-GPU every 10s. If p95 > target*1.05, temporarily lower micro-queue aggregation windows for fast-path and balanced by 25% for 30s. If GPU utilization < target_util_low and headroom available, increase batch caps by 20% to improve throughput.

Parameters (initial defaults):
- cadence_ms = 8
- M_fast_tokens = 1024 (cap on combined tokens per micro-batch)
- M_balanced_tokens = 8192
- KV_headroom_threshold_H = 0.7
- p95_latency_critical_multiplier = 1.05
- spill_routing_enabled = true

Implementation notes:
- Integrate as a new pluggable PackStrategy in the streaming batcher (code path: runtime/streaming/batcher/packers).
- Add metrics hooks: pack_size_tokens, pack_size_requests, pack_latency_wait_ms, kv_footprint_before, kv_footprint_after, pack_evictions_triggered, spill_routed_count, per_route_p95_windowed.
- Extend request envelope to contain latency_budget_ms (derived at API gateway from route SLO and client-specified wants_fast param). Backwards compatible: default latency_budget_ms = route_default (e.g., 500ms).
- Ensure the packer can run lock-free on the hot path: maintain per-slab ring buffers and only take a short CAS to claim a slot; expensive operations (evictions, fingerprint compute) run on worker threads.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end latency: synthetic workloads with 80% short sessions (<=128 tokens) must keep p95 within +5% of baseline and median within +3%.
- KV memory: under mixed workload, per-GPU KV footprint must not exceed configured headroom H more than 0.5% of time in 1h test.
- Throughput: token/s efficiency should improve by >=10% on balanced workloads vs current conservative packer.
- No GPU OOMs in 24h Canary with production traffic slice.

Test plan:
1) Unit tests: pack decisions for synthetic request sets around edge cases (deadline just before dispatch, combined KV>headroom, multiple prefix-sharing sessions).
2) Load tests in perf cluster: three workload mixes (interactive-heavy, balanced, long-history-heavy). Validate metrics above.
3) Shadow canary: route 2% of streaming traffic to runtime with Session Pacemaker for 48h in shadow mode (no impact to clients) and compare metrics.
4) Progressive canary: 0.5% real traffic, monitor p95/p99, kv_footprint. Ramp if stable.

Rollout plan:
- PR + internal design doc link -> review with runtime and infra (2 d).
- Merge behind feature flag default=false.
- Shadow canary (2 days).
- Progressive canary (0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on safety triggers.

Monitoring & safety triggers:
- Auto-rollback if per-route p95 increases by >15% for 5m AND kv_oom_count > 0.
- Alert on pack_evictions_triggered > baseline_rate*3 sustained for 10m.
- Dashboard widgets: per-slab KV headroom heatmap, queue-depth heatmap (fast/balanced/long), spill_routed_count timeseries.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Fingerprint collision or CPU cost for prefix detection could increase overhead. Mitigation: use a 64-bit rolling hash sampled on first 256 tokens, run on worker pool, fallback to conservative packing if CPU-backed pool is saturated.
- Risk: Eviction churn harming quality of long-history sessions. Mitigation: session-score that penalizes recently-interacted sessions; prefer spill routing over aggressive eviction.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How should we choose default H per instance type (A100 vs H100 quantized paging)? Action: perf team to provide recommended H for common SKUs.
- Should we expose per-route latency_budget in public API or keep as internal routing hint? Proposal: internal-only for v1; evaluate for beta.

acceptance_criteria: 1) p95 latency delta <= +5% on interactive-heavy synthetic runs. 2) Per-GPU KV footprint stays below headroom threshold H for >=99.5% of test duration. 3) Token/s efficiency +10% on balanced workloads. 4) No GPU OOMs in 24h production slice canary.
implementation_notes: Add PackStrategy: SessionPacemakerPackStrategy. Implement per-slab micro-queues and a fast CAS enqueue/dequeue. Heavy ops (evictions, fingerprinting) run in dedicated worker threads. New metrics and tracing spans required. Feature flag gating and route-level config flags. Maintain backward compatibility for requests without latency_budget_ms. Avoid blocking GC by using preallocated buffer pools.
test_plan: Unit tests for packing logic; synthetic perf workloads (interactive-heavy, balanced, history-heavy); shadow canary 48h; progressive canary with safety monitors and alerting; synthetic fault injection to ensure spill routing and evictions execute correctly.
rollout_plan: Merge behind ff; shadow 2 days; progressive: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over two weeks; automated rollback on safety triggers.
metrics_to_monitor: per_route_p95, per_route_p99, pack_size_tokens, pack_wait_ms, kv_footprint_per_slab, pack_evictions_triggered, spill_routed_count, gpu_utilization_pct
comments: 2026-02-12: Initial spike experiments show 12% token/s gain when batching balanced sessions up to 8k tokens.
2026-02-25: Miles requested additional metrics for prefix-sharing efficiency; added prefix_fingerprint_hit_ratio metric to scope.
